### MEDIUM: Docs adopt weaker serving\-authorization semantics while the threat model still assumes receipt\-required grants
[docs/architecture/security/attestation\.md:112](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/03456129d0dd5981ca8a5d1d74a233c6d4684016/docs/architecture/security/attestation.md#L112) · A-016, T-053, T-055, T-057, TB-011

The rewritten Context paragraph says a platform revision's basic serving no longer depends on recurring receipt or risk evidence\. It also allows an established identity to retain last\-known policy when administrative reads fail, up to the 'original proof and administrative ceilings'\. The base text and the canonical threat model assume the opposite\. The base attestation\.md required a verified current risk receipt with a complete metric for every grant\. T\-053 and T\-055 assume revocation and policy changes are read live, and T\-057 assumes grants fail when evidence is missing\. A revocation or qualification change made during an administrative\-read outage could therefore be honored late\. A provider with a lapsed receipt or risk metric could also keep serving\. The PR changes no threat\-model file even though its changelog claims to keep the retained threat model aligned\. The paragraph also leaves this repo's coordinator snapshot and the linked platform contract \(pinned to an external commit\) describing different grant rules\. Update T\-053, T\-055, T\-057 and TB\-011 to record the new ceilings, and state which implementation is authoritative\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: New endpoint\-resumption custody response is not covered by the threat model
[docs/architecture/security/attestation\.md:69](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/03456129d0dd5981ca8a5d1d74a233c6d4684016/docs/architecture/security/attestation.md#L69) · A-003, A-016, T-053, TB-002, TB-011

The PR adds a protocol\-1 endpoint\-custody response\. CoordinatorClient answers it synchronously, using the in\-memory X25519 key and a fresh nonce per socket\. A platform implementation can use the response to resume authorization with retained evidence across same\-process reconnects\. This adds a new proof\-of\-key\-custody message on TB\-002/TB\-011\. Its replay resistance, nonce and origin binding, and the rule that retained evidence may not extend proof deadlines are asserted only in prose\. The existing T\-053 \(replayed proof or stale authorization surviving connection change\) and TB\-011 do not describe a resume path\. A flawed platform implementation could let a replaced or hijacked connection inherit authorization, or let a reconnect lease outlive revocation\. Add a threat entry covering resumption and its deadline, revocation and nonce\-binding requirements\. Also add a conformance test requirement on the platform side\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### MEDIUM: Docs adopt platform semantics that drop the per\-grant fresh risk receipt and allow last\-known\-policy retention; threat model still asserts the stricter rule
[docs/architecture/security/attestation\.md:112](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/03456129d0dd5981ca8a5d1d74a233c6d4684016/docs/architecture/security/attestation.md#L112) · A-016, T-053, T-055, T-057, TB-011

The head text \(lines 10\-14, 112\) says the external darkbloom\-platform contract supersedes the retained coordinator snapshot\. Basic serving is no longer blocked by missing recurring receipt/risk evidence\. An established exact identity may retain last\-known policy within the original ceilings, and receipt monitoring is split from \`EvaluateAuthorization\`\. The canonical threat model still states that every serving grant needs a fresh verified risk receipt\. It also relies on failed reads never extending authorization \(T\-053, T\-057, TB\-011, A\-016\)\. A provider with a revoked or risky credential, or one whose receipt/risk evidence is withheld or failing, could keep serving under last\-known policy during admin\-read or receipt outages until the ceilings expire\. This is documented as the linked platform revision's behavior and not as deployed, so adoption is uncertain\. The threat model needs updating to state the new freshness and ceiling assumptions and how revocation fences interact with retained policy\. The docs should also say which repository enforces them, since the in\-repo coordinator snapshot is now explicitly non\-authoritative\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: New endpoint\-resumption custody response is attack surface not covered by the threat model
[docs/architecture/security/attestation\.md:69](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/03456129d0dd5981ca8a5d1d74a233c6d4684016/docs/architecture/security/attestation.md#L69) · A-016, T-053, T-054, TB-011

Head lines 69\-76 describe an \`app\_attest\_endpoint\_resumption\` candidate\. \`CoordinatorClient\` answers it directly with the fixed process key and a socket nonce, without Apple work\. A matching platform could then use that response together with retained evidence to resume or bind authorization to a new endpoint or connection\. This differs from the previously documented requirement for a fresh current\-endpoint assertion on every connection and endpoint binding\. The threat model does not cover the new surface: a replayed or misbound custody response, a proof signed by the process key alone with no hardware\-bound Apple freshness, a provider\-side oracle that signs coordinator\-supplied nonces, and deadline preservation\. The threat model should add this path to TB\-011, T\-053 and T\-054 and fix the required properties\. The nonce must be single\-use and bound to the connection and endpoint, original proof deadlines must not be extended, and revocation and qualification checks must be re\-run at resume\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: App Attest same\-process endpoint resumption is a new authorization\-adjacent path outside the threat model
[docs/architecture/security/identity\-binding\.md:110](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/03456129d0dd5981ca8a5d1d74a233c6d4684016/docs/architecture/security/identity-binding.md#L110) · A-016, T-053, T-057, TB-011

The new identity\-binding\.md section documents a provider\-side responder that answers a coordinator 'resume' challenge with the in\-memory X25519 key\. It also references backend 'retained\-proof' checks that are 'platform\-owned' and may not be deployed\. This is a new way to re\-establish a serving binding without a fresh Apple assertion\. TB\-011, T\-053 \(replayed proof or stale authorization after a connection change\) and T\-057 do not describe it\. Nothing in the model covers the nonce and socket binding, single use, the retained\-proof lifetime limit, the revocation fence, or the case where a provider ships the responder before the coordinator counterpart exists\. A stale or replayed resume challenge on a replacement socket, or a retained proof outliving revocation, would extend serving authorization\. Fix: add the resume path to TB\-011 and T\-053 with explicit invariants \(fresh per\-socket nonce, one answer, proof age cap, revocation and qualification\-generation recheck at final handoff, no lease extension\)\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: New provider\-token revocation endpoint and logout flow are not covered by the threat model
[docs/architecture/security/identity\-binding\.md:144](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/03456129d0dd5981ca8a5d1d74a233c6d4684016/docs/architecture/security/identity-binding.md#L144) · A-008, ADV-003, TB-002

Provider logout now sends the raw bearer token to POST /v1/device/revoke\. The docs say backend revocation policy and persistence are 'platform\-owned' and that local deletion cannot invalidate a copy held elsewhere, with an offline warning\. This adds an unauthenticated\-by\-session bearer\-in\-request control\-plane endpoint and a state where a deleted token stays valid on the coordinator\. A thief holding a copied provider token \(A\-008\) can keep registering as that account's provider, and the endpoint itself could be abused to revoke tokens if the token is leaked\. The model has no threat for provider\-token lifecycle: revoke endpoint rate\-limiting, token\-in\-body or header logging, revocation idempotency, immediate effect on live connections bound by B6, and what happens when offline logout leaves the token active\. Fix: add a threat and mitigations for A\-008 token revocation, including terminating or rebinding existing sessions on revocation\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Docs describe provider endpoint resumption across reconnect, but the App Attest threat model is not updated
[docs/developer/test\.md:51](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/03456129d0dd5981ca8a5d1d74a233c6d4684016/docs/developer/test.md#L51) · A-016, T-053, TB-011

The new test\.md sections describe 'Stage C' resumption: a provider reconnects after a 125\-second transport break with an unchanged process, endpoint and engine, and with 'unchanged load and Apple assertion counters'\. The canonical TB\-011, T\-053 and A\-016 say serving authorization is bound to one current connection and endpoint\. They also say each serving grant needs a fresh assertion and a new verified receipt, and that stale authorization must not survive a connection change\. A resume path that skips a new Apple assertion and re\-binds an old grant to a new socket \(only a 'fresh socket nonce'\) is a different trust transition\. A malicious provider \(ADV\-001\), or anyone holding a captured resume token or proof, could exploit it if the binding, expiry, reflection protection or revocation\-fencing rules are weak\. The PR changes only docs, so I cannot confirm the code\. TB\-011, T\-053 and the logout and credential\-revocation behaviour need explicit entries for resumption: what is authenticated, the maximum window, and how revocation or a policy\-generation change invalidates a resumable grant\. Suggested fix: update the threat model with these properties, or confirm in the docs that resumption never extends the grant lease and never survives revocation or a generation change\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### MEDIUM: Docs describe a recurring risk\-receipt policy that conflicts with the canonical serving requirement
[docs/provider/attestation\.md:85](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/03456129d0dd5981ca8a5d1d74a233c6d4684016/docs/provider/attestation.md#L85) · A-016, T-053, T-055, TB-011

The head text says a missing or unverified recurring risk receipt, or a missing risk metric, 'does not clear an accepted, otherwise valid basic serving grant'\. It also says no extra assertions are required\. It defers to a pinned external platform doc and adds that not every deployment uses the policy\. The canonical TB\-011 and the base docs require a verified fresh risk receipt for every serving grant, and receipt expiry and renewal deadlines shorten the grant\. If the platform coordinator follows the new text, grants could outlive receipt verification\. That weakens the credential\-continuity and revocation signal \(T\-053, T\-055\)\. Operators and reviewers also cannot tell which policy is live\. Fix: update TB\-011, A\-016 and T\-053/T\-055 to define the basic\-serving versus rewards/MDM\-removal receipt split and its bounds\. Alternatively, keep the docs aligned with the current requirement until that policy ships\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### MEDIUM: New endpoint\-resumption path serves without a fresh Apple call; not covered by the threat model
[docs/provider/attestation\.md:107](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/03456129d0dd5981ca8a5d1d74a233c6d4684016/docs/provider/attestation.md#L107) · A-016, T-053, T-054, TB-011

The added text describes a same\-process reconnect in which the provider answers an encrypted endpoint\-resumption challenge without another Apple call\. The platform then rechecks retained evidence and policy\. This creates a serving\-authorization path that skips fresh assertion verification, which TB\-011 treats as required \(assertion, nonce and counter, current endpoint and connection binding\)\. The docs themselves note the path is not enabled in production and rely on a report whose content was not supplied\. Risks include replaying or rebinding an old grant to a new connection, and extending a grant past the 15\-minute freshness window, past receipt expiry, or past revocation after a credential or build change \(T\-053, T\-054\)\. Fix: add the resumption protocol to TB\-011/T\-053, with explicit bounds on the maximum total lifetime without Apple proof, fencing by revocation and policy generation, endpoint\-key binding, and the final\-handoff check\. Keep it disabled until then\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

findings.detail: The new paragraph states that missing recurring receipt/risk evidence neither blocks otherwise qualified basic serving nor triggers further assertions. It also says only an established exact identity may retain last-known policy within proof and administrative ceilings. It cites an external darkbloom-platform revision for these semantics. The canonical threat model and the removed text require every serving grant to have a fresh verified risk receipt and complete metric. They also say failed reads never extend ceilings and that receipt renewal is independent. TB-011 and T-053/T-054/T-055/T-057 therefore no longer describe the cited authorization semantics. A provider whose receipt or risk evidence is missing or stale could now serve under the platform policy. Receipt-based Sybil, risk and capacity checks would then gate only rewards and MDM-removal readiness, not serving. The retained coordinator in this repo may still enforce the old rule, so the docs and the threat model now disagree. Fix: update TB-011, T-053..T-057 and A-016 to state which authorization authority applies. Define the retained-policy ceilings and the effect of missing receipts on serving. Mark the old receipt-required statements as superseded or snapshot-only.

findings.detail: The new logout flow sends the current saved provider token in `Authorization: Bearer` to `POST /v1/device/revoke` at the recorded issuer. The issuer is the original coordinator URL with only the WebSocket scheme changed. The doc does not say that HTTPS is required, that a `ws://` issuer is refused, or that `auth_token.issuer.json` is validated against an allowlist. If the provider was configured with a `ws://` coordinator or a tampered issuer file, the live A-008 provider token would be sent in cleartext or to the wrong host. Remote revocation is also best-effort (unconfirmed on any non-204) while the local copy is deleted, so a captured token can remain valid. The threat model has no entry for this new revoke endpoint or the issuer-binding file. Fix: refuse non-TLS and non-allowlisted issuers (loopback excepted) and document the revoke endpoint under the provider-token threats (T-039/A-008).
findings.title: Logout sends the raw provider bearer token to a URL derived from the stored coordinator URL; transport security is unspecified

findings.detail: A hidden `--native-serve-qualification-v1` entry now runs a separate AppKit host with the real signed app identity and the App Attest and encrypted-inference paths. It is gated by `DARKBLOOM_NATIVE_SERVE_QUALIFICATION=1`, a literal 127.0.0.1 WebSocket, and owner-only inputs. TB-011 and A-015/A-016 do not mention this mode. Open questions: whether it shares the production App Attest key, Keychain item or generation budget; whether plaintext `ws://` loopback traffic with a local harness coordinator can expose assertions or prompts; and whether the env-var gate is enforced before any Apple call. A malicious or compromised local process could set the env var and drive the official binary against a fake coordinator to burn credential budgets or harvest proofs. Fix: document the entry in the TB-011 threat model, and ensure it uses an isolated credential namespace, is compiled out of or refused in production builds, and cannot reach non-loopback hosts.
